title: Security governance, uptime SLA & escalation workshop with Bluecliff Capital
topics: Data residency and VPC private control plane
Incident response, BCDR (RTO/RPO) and escalation runbooks
Uptime SLA targets and fallback behavior
next_steps: Redwood to share SOC 2 Type II summary + SOC2 bridge doc (Maya)
SE to run a scoped failover tabletop with Bluecliff SREs (Connor/Evan)
Provide encryption/KMS whitepaper and HSM partner docs
Draft SLA appendix for Dedicated plan and proposed RTO/RPO numbers
action_items: Maya: email SOC2 bridge + compliance packet by 2026-10-01
Connor: schedule tabletop DR run with Bluecliff SREs for week of 2026-10-11
Diego: share KMS architecture diagram and supported HSM vendors by 2026-10-05
Evan/Marcus: provide internal RTO/RPO acceptability matrix and top 3 app owners contact by 2026-10-04

transcript:
Meeting Start: 2026-09-28 16:00 PDT
Duration (recorded): 62 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Connor (Redwood SE), Diego (Redwood SE), Anya (Bluecliff CISO), Marcus (Head of Platform), Priya (Legal), Evan (SRE)

Summary: Quick sync to validate Redwood's SOC 2 posture, KMS/encryption options for private deployments, and to walk through incident escalation and BCDR runbook expectations. Bluecliff wants clear RTO/RPO numbers and an SLA exhibit for Dedicated deployment; also needs assurance on audit log retention and SSO onboarding timeline.

00:00:06 - Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda, we'll do a short overview of our compliance artifacts, run through SSO/RBAC options, then Connor will take you through the planned RTO/RPO and failover model. save time at end for priya's procurement questions.
00:00:22 - Anya: thanks maya, yeah high level we're prepping for internal audit in q1 and procurement wants the SLA and key security docs by mid-october.
00:00:35 - Marcus: also want to understand impact on our latency profiles if we route to dedicated vs hosted fallback. cost vs availability tradeoffs.
00:00:47 - Connor: totally, we'll cover routing policies and model variant fallbacks, and how we do graceful degradation.

00:01:30 - Maya: okay first, SOC 2. we are SOC 2 Type II, our audit firm is Lumen & Gray, and we have a SOC2 report + bridge letter that covers recent infra changes, we'll share the redacted copy.
00:01:46 - Priya: when you say bridge letter, is that the item that shows controls gaps for changes since the last assessment? we need that for our legal.
00:01:58 - Maya: yes exactly, bridge doc + control mapping to bluecliff's control framework. we'll include a mapping sheet.
00:02:12 - Anya: do you also have ISO22301 or ISO27001 artifacts? we've got some teams that require ISO.
00:02:20 - Maya: not ISO27001 certified today, we're SOC 2 focused; we have external assessments and an ISO-aligned controls matrix we can share, but not cert.

00:03:05 - Marcus: SSO — what's the onboarding cadence? we use Okta and JumpCloud for some corp units.
00:03:15 - Diego: we support SAML and OIDC, Okta is a first-class path. typical onboarding takes 2-3 business days for SAML metadata exchange + test accounts, longer if you want SCIM provisioning.
00:03:28 - Evan: for RBAC, can you map to our internal teams? like environment-level roles and ability to restrict model access per team?
00:03:38 - Connor: yes we have role scoping at the org, project, model and route level, and token-level restrictions. it's policy driven. sometimes the export labels in our console are slightly different in the transcript (note: small transcription issue).

00:04:50 - Marcus: audit logs — retention and format? we need immutable logs for 2 years and an ability to stream to our SIEM.
00:05:00 - Diego: logs can be retained in platform for up to 24 months depending on plan; we produce structured JSON events and you can forward a stream to your SIEM via a secure syslog or S3 push, plus we support Kafka for enterprise customers.
00:05:16 - Anya: are logs redacted by default for PII? we have strict PII rules.
00:05:24 - Connor: we do sensitive data redaction for hosted by default and for Dedicated/Private you can configure redaction policies; we also support prefix caching so PII can be masked in prompts before storage. (note: "K V cache" in earlier notes may appear as KV cache).

00:06:45 - Priya: encryption — where are keys stored and who manages keys? we need BYOK and HSM-backed options.
00:06:55 - Diego: we offer three patterns: provider-managed keys, customer-managed keys (CMK) in cloud KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault), and HSM-backed BYOK for Private/on-prem installations. for Dedicated we can integrate with your KMS via cross account grants.
00:07:12 - Priya: and what's the key rotation policy and audit?
00:07:18 - Diego: rotation is configurable; we log key usage events and can provide key access audit logs; HSM vendors we integrate with include Thales and AWS CloudHSM.

00:08:40 - Anya: data residency — can we pin customer data + inference to eu-west regions only and ensure the control plane doesn't see plaintext?
00:08:50 - Connor: yes for Private/VPC deployments control plane can be customer-managed; for hosted we have region pinning and we can commit to residency controls in the SLA. note: control plane access to plaintext is limited and we support envelope encryption so service only sees encrypted blobs unless you choose to allow managed keys.
00:09:10 - Marcus: good. what's the network model for private deployments — do we do private endpoints and VPC peering?
00:09:18 - Diego: we support VPC peering, private link equivalents in each cloud, and an option for full on-prem bundle with customer-managed control plane.

00:10:25 - Connor: moving to incident response and BCDR. typical options: active-active across regions with automatic failover, active-passive with warm standby, and dedicated reserved pools with SLA-backed failover. want to align on RTO/RPO tolerances.
00:10:40 - Evan: our top apps are trade-alerts (low-latency, RTO < 30s ideally) and portfolio-sync (RTO < 10 min). RPO tolerances vary, but for trade-alerts RPO must be near-zero.
00:10:58 - Connor: for near-zero RPO we recommend dedicated reserved pools with synchronous replication of state (prefix/KV cache) + hotspots pinned to regional shards. for more relaxed RPO (minutes) you can rely on async KV replication and accept short replay windows.

00:12:05 - Marcus: if a GPU cluster becomes unavailable, what's the graceful degradation path? do you drop to smaller model variant or route to other region?
00:12:15 - Connor: we have a routing policy engine: first try same-region dedicated, then fallback to cross-region dedicated, then hosted best-effort with reduced QoS (e.g., smaller model, quantized variant). these transitions are logged as part of the audit trail.

00:13:40 - Anya: SLA numbers — what uptime can you commit for Dedicated vs Hosted?
00:13:48 - Maya: Hosted is currently 99.9% for the platform, Dedicated comes with an SLA exhibit up to 99.95% depending on commitment tier. we can draft an appendix with credits and escalation SLAs.
00:14:05 - Priya: credits aside, we also need defined RTO windows and a transparent escalation ladder to our ops.
00:14:12 - Maya: yes, our escalation ladder includes oncall triage, SE oncall, engineering pager, and exec escalation. we'll put names/times in the SLA appendix.

00:15:30 - Evan: who actually runs the DR failover? internal SREs or Redwood can run failover in partnership?
00:15:40 - Connor: we support both models: self-service runbook that your SRE can execute, or Redwood-assisted failover where we run the steps under a pre-agreed playbook. we recommend a joint tabletop first.
00:16:05 - Marcus: how often do you run DR tests with customers?
00:16:12 - Diego: cadence is quarterly for Dedicated customers who ask; otherwise annual. tests include synthetic traffic, prefix cache replay, and model warmup checks.

00:17:25 - Anya: can you provide a sample incident runbook and an example post-mortem that redwood has produced?
00:17:33 - Maya: yes will attach our incident runbook + anonymized post-mortem for a previous region failover where we did a canary rollback and model variant fallback.

00:18:50 - Priya: legal question — are audit logs admissible and do you provide chain of custody? we need to ensure logs are tamper evident.
00:18:58 - Diego: logs are write-once in our storage tier and we can provide signed digests / checksums on export; for Dedicated we can enable append-only object storage in your account for full custody.

00:20:30 - Marcus: operational question — token-level cost breakdowns, how fast can we get per-route latency metrics during an incident?
00:20:38 - Connor: tracing hooks expose per-request timing and model-level token timing; in an incident you can open a tracing window and we can provide a CSV export within 24 hours, and a dashboard snapshot immediately.

00:22:00 - Anya: escalation process — lay out the steps again please, including who to call and when?
00:22:08 - Maya: 1) customer files incident in portal or calls main line — automatic triage creates a Sev1 if threshold met; 2) Redwood oncall triage engages SE and engineering; 3) 15 minute SLA to contact customer for Sev1; 4) if not resolved in agreed RTO, we ramp to exec escalation. we'll include times in appendix.
00:22:40 - Evan: what's the expected notification method? we prefer pager duty + email.
00:22:45 - Diego: we integrate with PagerDuty and can push to your service.

00:24:10 - Marcus: pricing impact — if we require reserved capacity + cross-region replication that's a higher tier, correct?
00:24:20 - Maya: yes reserved capacity and replication increase cost; Redwood Optimize can help estimate unit economics. we'll provide a model for cost vs RTO/RPO to help tradeoff decisions.

00:27:00 - Priya: procurement checklist items — we need SOC2, BAA if PHI involved (not in this case), a DPA, and SLA appendix. you confirm you can sign our standard DPA with minor edits?
00:27:10 - Maya: we can work with your legal, we do standard DPA and will review the change list.

00:29:45 - Connor: quick tech note: KV cache persistence is stored on NVRAM-backed volumes and replicates to secondary region asynchronously by default, can be configured for sync depending on perf cost.
00:30:02 - Anya: any single points of failure for the control plane in private deployment?
00:30:10 - Diego: for Private with customer-managed control plane it's your responsibility; for Redwood-managed Private we run HA control plane across zones and provide documented failover steps.

00:33:00 - Maya: ok let's recap next steps and owners. i'll share SOC2 + bridge doc, SEs will schedule tabletop, Diego will send KMS diagram and HSM vendor list, and we'll draft SLA appendix with RTO/RPO options.
00:33:20 - Priya: thanks, and please include a sample contract clause for indemnities around data residency.
00:33:28 - Maya: will do.

00:34:10 - Marcus: one last question on monitoring — can we keep a mirrored telemetry stream in our observability tenant?
00:34:18 - Connor: yes we support telemetry forwarding to your datadog/newrelic/elk stack; for Dedicated we can run an agent in your VPC forwarding encrypted metrics.

00:35:45 - Anya: great this was useful. suggests we start with the tabletop next week and then decide on reserved capacity sizing after the test.
00:35:55 - Evan: yep i'll coordinate internal app owners for the tabletop.

00:36:30 - Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the packet and proposed dates.
00:36:36 - (call ends; short crosstalk)

Post-call notes: action items captured above; transcription has occasional speaker attribution noise and a few mis-heard acronyms ("SAMEL" instead of SAML in one segment). Recommend Redwood SEs prepare a concise one-page RTO/RPO exhibit to attach to the SLA appendix.

Meeting End.
